weather_report:
Subiaco slips past midnight under a quilt of broken cloud, the stars smudged and shy, the streets holding a faint shine. It is not a night for sun; UV is essentially asleep, and the air feels gentled, a touch introspective. Toward the small hours those clouds are likely to fatten into a light, passing rain, soft enough to patter and move on. Clarity is muted rather than murky, with edges blurred and sounds carrying a little farther than usual.

Daybreak looks subdued and a little damp, with sunshine filtered and hesitant; UV will stay low at first and only sharpen if the cover breaks later on. A light layer and shoes you don’t mind on wet pavement will serve you well, and a compact rain shell wouldn’t be amiss. If you’re awake, this is a good time to tidy the last corners of the kitchen, set tomorrow’s bag by the door, or read a few calm pages while the town hushes around you. In the morning, keep errands simple and close to home; a short tram ride for bread and a newspaper, then a quiet coffee by the window while the sky decides what it wants to do.
